questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: The founding of the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown
The history of the Baltimore Orioles under Ned Hanlon
The 1938 Giants season and the team's exhibition tours
McGraw's life and the Truxton sites honoring him
questions.explain: It covers McGraw's career and the monument, ballfield and sign commemorating him in Truxton.

questions.q: Why did McGraw run away from home?
options: He was offered a place on a professional team and left to play elsewhere
He ran away to work for the Elmira, Cortland and Northern Railroad selling goods
His father became physically abusive after the family lost several members to disease
A neighbor persuaded his father to let the boy live with her and her two sons
questions.explain: The passage says his father became abusive after the diphtheria deaths, prompting McGraw to run away.

questions.q: What was the purpose of the 1938 exhibition game in Truxton?
options: To serve as the Giants' final spring training game before the season
To raise money for a monument to McGraw in Truxton
To recruit local players into professional baseball
To celebrate the opening of John J. McGraw Field
questions.explain: The friendly match was scheduled to raise funds for a monument to the local lad who never returned.

questions.q: What was McGraw's nickname, and why?
options: The Old Professor, for teaching hitters new batting tactics
Iron Man, for playing through injuries for seventeen years
Little Napoleon, for calling every pitch and ruling his players
The Peerless Leader, for winning ten pennants in a row
questions.explain: He was called Little Napoleon for calling every pitch and telling players how to live.

questions.q: What does the passage imply about McGraw and Truxton?
options: He was buried in Truxton beside his mother
He never returned to his hometown after leaving in 1890
He often visited Truxton during the Giants' spring tours
He retired to Truxton after managing the Giants
questions.explain: He never returned to his hometown after leaving in 1890 to play baseball.
